faq.title: Most Common Questions
faq.subtitle: Answers to frequently asked questions about our technicum

item1.question: How is admission to the technicum conducted?
item1.answer: Admission is conducted online via the my.edu.uz portal or directly through the technicum admissions committee. 9th and 11th grade graduates are accepted.

item2.question: Is there a tuition fee?
item2.answer: Education is organized on both state grant (free of charge) and contract-fee bases. Talented youth study free of charge under state education grants.

item3.question: What study programs and specialties are offered?
item3.answer: Full-time programs: Digital Information Processing Master, Computer Networks and IT Service, Fashion and Tailoring, Electrician, Chemical Fibers, Electric Bus and Electric Vehicle Service, Residential Infrastructure, Hairdressing (Stylist). Dual education programs: Fashion and Tailoring, Electrician, Electric Vehicle Service, Renewable Energy Maintenance.

item4.question: What opportunities exist after graduating from the technicum?
item4.answer: Graduates receive a state-recognized diploma. With this diploma, they can work at industrial enterprises or enroll into 2nd-year university programs based on interview assessment.

item5.question: What extracurricular clubs are available?
item5.answer: Free clubs operate in our technicum: 'Young Programmers', 'Robotics', 'Electrical Engineering', 'Auto Workshop', 'English Club', and sports sections.

item6.question: Where is the technicum located?
item6.answer: Our technicum is located at 170 Fergana Street, Fergana City (the former Oil and Gas Industry College building). Easily accessible by public transport.

about.historyP1: Fergana City Technicum No. 5 was established to provide regional 9th grade graduates and youth with modern vocational education in technical, engineering, and service fields. Over the years, the institution has educated thousands of skilled specialists.
about.historyP2: Advanced educational curricula have been introduced in Information Technology, Engineering and Mechanics, Electrical Engineering, and Socio-Economic disciplines.
about.historyP3: Today, the technicum maintains strong ties with modern industrial enterprises, allowing students to learn theory and practice hand in hand.
